comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks a DRG 80 gripper opening stop at 90° and verifies retained motion; PR-2253 strikes a safety match, lights a candle, and disposes of the match safely.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests concentric two-tool screw/jam-nut adjustment, bimanual countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated-cycle verification. PR-2253 tests stabilizing a matchbox, controlled match striking, flame-to-wick placement and dwell, and safe burning-match transfer. Shared bimanual manipulation is only generic.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked opening within angular tolerances, retained nuts, three repeatable cycles with limited drift, and hands/tools clear. PR-2253 requires force/speed/distance-gated ignition, wick-proximity and ignition dwells, the lit candle upright, the spent match in the ashtray, the box down, and hands clear, with fire-specific zero/cap failures. Both available spec versions provide these rubric details.
comparison.reason: The tasks test meaningfully different mechanisms and abilities: preserving a mechanical adjustment against locknut reaction and proving repeatable motion versus producing and managing ignition through a struck match. Neither objective nor its defining physical skill or terminal outcome substantially overlaps.
